title: Hark Handoff² Launches: 2x Faster Computer-Use Agent
summary: Hark releases Handoff², a computer-use agent inside Hark Pro that completes tasks 2x faster with 82% success rate on 478 internal web benchmarks.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Hark launched Handoff², a second-generation computer-use agent inside Hark Pro that executes web tasks twice as fast as its predecessor.
- The agent achieved an 82% completion rate across 478 internal web task benchmarks by learning to batch multiple actions per inference cycle.
- Latency-penalized reinforcement learning trained Handoff² to minimize round trips, cutting average task completion time in half while maintaining reliability.


Hark has officially launched Handoff², the second-generation[computer-use agent](https://emergent.sh/glossary/computer-use-agent) powering Hark Pro, delivering a 2x speed improvement over its predecessor. Officially released on November 16, 2026, the agent completes 82% of 478 internal web task benchmarks while cutting average execution time in half through learned action batching and latency-penalized reinforcement learning.


## Performance Gains Through Action Batching


Handoff² achieves its speed advantage by executing multiple interface actions within a single inference cycle, reducing the number of round trips required to complete a web task. Where the original Handoff typically issued one action per model call, the new agent learned to group related steps such as form fills, button clicks, and navigation commands into coordinated batches. This architectural shift directly addresses the latency bottleneck that computer-use agents face when orchestrating browser interactions through repeated API calls.


The 82% completion rate across Hark's 478-task internal benchmark represents a balance between speed and reliability. Tasks ranged from multi-step form submissions to cross-page data extraction workflows, testing the agent's ability to maintain context and recover from partial failures while executing batched commands.


## Latency-Penalized Reinforcement Learning


Hark trained Handoff² using a reinforcement learning loop that explicitly penalized wall-clock latency alongside task success metrics. Traditional RL objectives for computer-use agents optimize for correctness or step efficiency, but Handoff²'s reward function incorporated real-world timing constraints. This pushed the model to favor strategies that minimized inference round trips even when single-action approaches might have been simpler to execute.


The latency penalty forced the agent to develop predictive heuristics about which actions could safely be batched without intermediate validation. For example, filling a multi-field form and clicking submit can often be combined if the agent has high confidence in field values, whereas navigation to a new page typically requires waiting for a load event before proceeding. Handoff² learned these distinctions during training rather than relying on hard-coded rules.


## Integration With Hark Pro


Handoff² ships as the default computer-use agent inside Hark Pro, Hark's enterprise automation platform. Users interact with the agent through natural language task descriptions, and Handoff² translates those instructions into browser automation sequences. The 2x speed improvement means workflows that previously took 40 seconds now complete in roughly 20 seconds, a difference that compounds across hundreds of daily task executions in production environments.


Hark has not disclosed whether Handoff² will be made available outside the Hark Pro subscription tier or as a standalone API. The agent currently operates within Hark's managed browser environment, which provides sandboxing and session management infrastructure that desktop computer-use agents lack.


## What This Means


Handoff²'s launch signals a maturation phase for computer-use agents, where incremental performance gains and production reliability take priority over raw capability expansion. The shift from single-action to batched execution models represents a practical optimization that other agent frameworks will likely adopt as latency becomes a competitive differentiator. For Hark Pro users, the speed improvement translates directly into faster workflow automation and lower operational costs per completed task, making browser-based agents more economically viable for high-volume use cases.
